question: Where can I get the list of grid connection requests in Spain, with project, technology, capacity (MW), connection node, status and date?

answer.summary: No single national list of grid connection requests with project, technology, MW, node, status and date exists in what was checked. REE publishes monthly (xlsx/pdf) the individual requests for demand and storage-as-consumption at transport nodes >=220 kV (ID, date, node, position, MW; no project name). Generation and distribution queues appear only aggregated per node/position (REE CSV, CNMC ArcGIS layers, distributor CSVs) or per technology and region (REE GW PDF).
main_caveats: The REE demand list covers only demand and storage acting as consumption at nodes >=220 kV; it is not the generation queue and has no project names.
Generation queue is aggregated (GW by technology and region, MW by node/position); never sum node values: CNMC says capacities are not directly additive.
The REE demand list is valid one month (publication to 'Fecha fin del mes de publicacion'); older months stay downloadable by changing the month in the file name.
Distribution-level requests: only 'admitted and unresolved' MW per substation bar (CNMC and distributor files); over 300 distributors exist per CNMC, 61 appear in the CNMC layer.
answer.confidence_reason: Core files opened and tested; negatives rest on REE, CNMC, MITECO and e-distribucion pages. REE interactive map data endpoint not found; other distributors and regions only sampled.

how_to_use.example_request: curl -sL -o dem_oct.xlsx "https://www.ree.es/sites/default/files/12_CLIENTES/Documentos/publicacion-solicitudes-acceso-demanda-octubre-2026.xlsx"  # sheet 'Listado de solicitudes', header on row 6, data from row 7
how_to_use.example_result: Row 7: GENT-53853-26 | received 46254 (Excel serial = 2026-08-20) | 'Solicitud de almacenamiento conectado a la red de transporte que consume energia de la red.' | ALVARADO 220 | AVR220-SCAL | Extremadura | 46 MW | 46341 (2026-11-15) | NO. File has 36 requests (25 storage, 11 consumption), 1,942.6 MW in total.
steps: Open the 'Landing' page and take the .xlsx link of the current month; the file name pattern is publicacion-solicitudes-acceso-demanda-<mes>-<aaaa>.xlsx.
Read sheet 'Listado de solicitudes': row 3-4 hold publication and closing dates; row 6 headers; rows 7+ requests.
Convert Excel serial dates (1899-12-30 origin) to dates; MW uses '.' as decimal in xlsx cells (the PDF shows commas).
Earlier months can be fetched by changing the month in the URL (tested: agosto-2026, septiembre-2026, enero-2026, diciembre-2025, mayo-2026 return 200; agosto-2025 and octubre-2025 return 404).
reading_traps: It is a demand/storage list, not a generation queue: no project name, no promoter, no technology other than 'storage' vs 'consumption'.
The 'Leyenda' sheet still shows publication/closing dates of 2025 (18 August 2025 / 12 August 2025) while the data sheet says 15 and 6 October 2026.
Several requests can share a node with the same MW on different positions (May 2026 PDF: DEA-50689-26 and DEA-50694-26, 885 MW each at ARCOS DE LA FRONTERA 400); do not sum blindly.
Reception dates can be months before the closing date (request received 2026-08-20, list closed 2026-10-06): the list holds requests admitted to processing, not requests received that month.

problems: Server rejects HEAD requests with 403 (Incapsula); GET works with default curl identification.

steps: Download the CSV of the month from the REE 'Conoce la capacidad de acceso' page of generator or consumer.
Rows 1-2 are grouped headers; data start in row 3; separator ';' and BOM; numbers use ',' as decimal and '.' as thousands separator.
For per-position detail read Generacion_por_posicion.pdf with pdftotext -layout (columns En servicio, Pendiente de puesta en servicio, En curso, each split MGES/MPE).
Join node names with CNMC layers (source 4) to get coordinates.
reading_traps: No project name, promoter or request date: values are aggregated by node or position.
Whether 'otorgada' includes plants already in service is not stated in the CSV; only the position PDF separates the states.
In the PDF some cells are empty rather than 0 and values shift between MGES and MPE columns in text extraction: check against the page image.
Node values are not additive across nodes (CNMC warning).

steps: The layers are found in the item data of the CNMC ArcGIS Experience apps (https://www.arcgis.com/sharing/rest/content/items/<experience id>/data?f=json): Generacion app 0dac803d644f41519fdd11da11ef10ae, Demanda app c7dc433cb2e44d53a908a8a467523f5a.
Query with where=1=1, outFields and resultRecordCount; add outSR=4326 for lon/lat (tested: all 937 transport points fall inside Spain's bounding box).
Filter CAP_ADMITIDA_NO_RESUELTA>0 to list nodes with requests pending evaluation.
reading_traps: These are node-level aggregates; no request, promoter or project date.
Point geometry is the substation (Web Mercator by default), not the plant.
Layer ids differ between services (0, 4, 11, 10): index 0 does not exist in the distribution and period services.
The service is the data behind a viewer; the CNMC page does not document it as a public API and gives no licence.

recipe: 1. Get the BOE daily summary: curl -sL -H 'Accept: application/json' https://www.boe.es/datosabiertos/api/boe/sumario/AAAAMMDD (tested for 20260911: 131 items).
2. Keep items whose 'titulo' mentions 'autorizacion administrativa' and 'MW'; the title already gives project, MW and province (e.g. BOE-A-2026-19045 'Alto Cabrera' 144 MW, a refusal).
3. Download url_pdf.texto and run pdftotext -layout; read the first page for promoter, filing date, technology and the evacuation text (tested on BOE-B-2026-29448: node 'Carmona 220 kV').
4. Match the node name to the REE per-node/position files (source 2) or CNMC layers (source 4) to see aggregated MW at that node.
5. For tender nodes, read the BOE order (e.g. Orden TED/578/2026) for awarded MW and promoter.
if_unstructured.location_method: Substation coordinates come from the CNMC ArcGIS layers (source 4) or e-distribucion UTM columns (source 5); notices give municipality and sometimes polygon coordinates in annexes (not checked).
